paragraphs.en: According to the {Solar} Energy Industry Association, the number of solar {panels} installed has grown rapidly over the past decade.Solar panel installation has been increasing both at the {county} level and in {overseas} projects.Countries in {Europe} , North {America} , and parts of Asia have been particularly active in promoting solar energy.The governments' clear {agenda} to promote green energy has made solar panel installation an attractive {investment} .As a result, solar panels are found both in urban areas and {suburbs} , although the {percentage} of people who are able to afford solar panels remains relatively low.All of that growth will {occupy} a lot of space.The panels have caused some new environmental issues, including {damage} to farmland and concerns about energy {coverage} .Though more and more people accept the concept of solar energy, few like large solar panels to be installed near them.
paragraphs.cn: 据 <u> 太阳 </u> 能行业协会称，在过去十年中，太阳能 <u> 电池板 </u> 的安装数量迅速增长。无论是在 <u> 县 </u> 域层面，还是在 <u> 海外 </u> 项目中，太阳能电池板的安装量都在不断增加。 <u> 欧洲 </u> 、北 <u> 美洲 </u> 和亚洲部分地区的国家在推广太阳能方面尤为积极。各政府提出明确的 <u> 议程 </u> ，大力推广绿色能源，让安装太阳能电池板成为一项颇具吸引力的 <u> 投资 </u> 。因此，尽管有能力安装太阳能电池板的人群 <u> 占比 </u> 仍然相对较低，但太阳能电池板在城市和 <u> 郊区 </u> 都随处可见。所有这些增长都将 <u> 占用 </u> 大量空间。太阳能电池板引发了一些新的环境问题，包括对耕地的 <u> 破坏 </u> 和对能源 <u> 覆盖范围 </u> 的担忧。虽然越来越多的人接受了太阳能这一概念，但很少有人愿意让大型太阳能电池板安装在自家附近。

paragraphs.en: Solar {developers} want to put up panels as quickly and {cheaply} as possible, so they haven't given much thought to what they put under them.Often, they'll end up {abandoning} these lands by covering them with small {stones} and using chemicals to control weeds.The result is that many communities, especially in {farming} regions, {criticize} solar {stations} as {destroyers} of {crops} and the soil, causing a {crash} in local ecosystems.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳能 <u> 开发商 </u> 希望尽快且 <u> 低成本地 </u> 安装太阳能电池板，所以他们并未过多考虑太阳能电池板下方的土地会受到什么影响。通常，他们会在这些土地上铺满小 <u> 石子 </u> ，并用化学药剂除草，最终对土地造成了 <u> 遗弃 </u> 般的破坏。结果就是，许多社区，尤其是在 <u> 务农 </u> 地区， <u> 指责 </u> 太阳能发电 <u> 站破坏农作物 </u> 和土壤，导致当地生态系统出现 <u> 崩溃 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: “Solar projects need to be good neighbors,”says Jordan Macknick, the head of the {Innovative} Site {Preparation} and Impact Reductions on the Environment (InSPIRE) project.“They need to be {protectors} of the land and contribute to the {agricultural} economy.”InSPIRE is {investigating} practical approaches to “low-impact” solar development, which focuses on {establishing} and {operating} solar farms in a way that is kinder to the land.They have {hatched} a low-impact solar strategy, which is to provide {habitat} for pollinators ( (传粉昆虫) ).By introducing {herbs} , wildflowers, and other native plants under solar panels, solar farms can effectively provide a shelter for these important insects.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 创新 </u> 场地 <u> 筹备 </u> 及环境影响减少项目（InSPIRE）的负责人乔丹·麦克尼克说：“太阳能项目应该与周边和谐共处。它们应该成为土地的 <u> 守护者 </u> ，并为 <u> 农业 </u> 经济做出贡献。”InSPIRE项目正在 <u> 研究 </u> “低影响”太阳能开发的可行方法，重点是以对土地更友好的方式 <u> 建设 </u> 和 <u> 运营 </u> 太阳能农场。他们 <u> 策划 </u> 了一项低影响太阳能战略——为授粉昆虫提供 <u> 栖息地 </u> 。通过在太阳能电池板下种植 <u> 草本植物 </u> 、野花和其他本地植物，太阳能农场能够有效地为这些重要昆虫提供庇护所。

paragraphs.en: Habitat loss, {pesticide} use, and climate change have caused dramatic declines in pollinator populations over the past couple of decades, damaging the {US} agricultural economy. {Conservation} {administrations} put out pollinator-friendliness {guidelines} for home gardens, {enterprises} , schools, cities—and now there are guidelines for solar farm {sponsors} .
paragraphs.cn: 在过去的几十年里，栖息地的丧失、 <u> 杀虫剂 </u> 的使用以及气候变迁导致授粉昆虫的数量急剧减少，破坏了 <u> 美国 </u> 的农业经济。 <u> 保护管理部门 </u> 针对家庭花园、 <u> 企业单位 </u> 、学校和城市发布了授粉昆虫友好 <u> 指导方针 </u> ——现在，针对太阳能农场 <u> 赞助商 </u> 也制定了相关指导方针。

paragraphs.en: In terms of {ecology} , these solar pollinator projects create {networks} of green spaces that can cover vast regions, linking smaller plots of habitat that may otherwise be {isolated} .As the {Pacific} region experiences shifts in climate, they can help sustain healthy pollinator populations through seasonal movements or droughts.
paragraphs.cn: 从 <u> 生态学 </u> 角度来看，这些授粉昆虫项目创建了覆盖大片区域的绿地空间 <u> 网络 </u> ，将原本各自 <u> 孤立 </u> 的小块栖息地连接起来。随着 <u> 太平洋 </u> 地区气候发生变化，这些项目有助于维持健康的授粉昆虫种群的数量，使其免受季节性迁徙或干旱的影响。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
